topic.title: TypeScript — Quick Revision
topic.subtitle: Types, generics and utility types you are expected to know.

questions.q: What is TypeScript and why use it?

answer.value: TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript that compiles to plain JS. Types are checked at compile time, catching bugs early, enabling autocomplete and safe refactoring. They are erased at runtime, so there is no runtime cost.

questions.q: interface vs type — what is the difference?

items: Both describe object shapes and can be extended.
`interface` supports declaration merging and `extends`; best for public object contracts and classes.
`type` can also name unions, tuples, primitives and mapped/conditional types.
`unknown` is the type-safe `any`: you must narrow it before use.
`never` is a value that can't exist (function that always throws, exhausted union).

answer.value: Generics let a function, class or type work with many types while keeping them linked, instead of using `any`.

questions.q: What are union and intersection types?

items: `A | B` — a value is either A or B.
`A & B` — a value has all members of A and B.

answer.value:
type Id = string | number;
type Admin = User & { permissions: string[] };
TypeScript narrows a union inside a branch using `typeof`, `instanceof`, `in`, equality checks, truthiness, or a discriminant property. User-defined guards use `x is T`.

items: `Pick<T, K>` / `Omit<T, K>` — choose or drop keys.
`Record<K, V>` — object with keys K and values V.

questions.q: Optional properties, readonly, and the non-null assertion?

items: `value!` — tells the compiler it isn't null/undefined; unchecked, so use sparingly.

questions.q: What is enum and what are alternatives?

answer.value: `enum` creates a named set of constants (numeric by default; string enums are safer). A lighter alternative is a union of literals — `type Role = 'admin' | 'user'` — which has no runtime code.
`strict: true` turns on a group of checks including `strictNullChecks`, `noImplicitAny`, `strictFunctionTypes` and `strictPropertyInitialization`. It's the recommended default for new projects.

questions.q: What are mapped and conditional types?

answer.value:
type Flags<T> = { [K in keyof T]: boolean };       // mapped
type IsString<T> = T extends string ? 'yes' : 'no'; // conditional
Combined with `infer` they power utilities such as `ReturnType`.

questions.q: keyof, typeof and indexed access types?
How do you type React props and hooks?
as assertions vs type guards vs satisfies?

answer.value: `as` forces a type and can lie. A type guard proves it at runtime. `satisfies` checks that a value matches a type **without widening** its inferred type.
TypeScript compares types by shape, not by name. Any object with the required properties is assignable, even if it was never declared as that type.
